messages.subject: Re: Detection history (CamtrapR)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
check the argument  recordDateTimeFormat. It is not specified correctly.

My guess is that you opened the record table csv in Excel and saved it. Excel tends to reformat dates and then save the formatted version, which has the order jumbled up and omits the secons.

There is 3 different things you can do:

1. Reconstruct the original DateTimeOriginal column by combining the date and time columns via:

 paste(Go_green$Date, Go_green$Time, sep = " ")

2. Change the recordDateTimeFormat argument to %d/%m/%Y %H:%M"

3. Rerun the record table function and then don't save edits in Excel.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Nitpakone,

I am not sure if this would help, but unless you have set your working directory to the folder where these two excel files are saved, R cannot find the file. For example:
setwd(C:/This/is/where/my/files/are/saved)

Alternatively. Try typing in the whole directory as the argument to the the read.csv function. For example:
camtraps <- read.csv(C:/This/is/where/my/files/are/saved/HNN_Phouchueng_NOV2017.csv)

When you load your camera traps file into R sometimes R can change the columns to class factor if you don't specify so always make sure that the station and camera columns are of class character. You can then check if the columns are of the right class by running this code:
str(camtrapsMara)

If they are not of class character then use the code below to change then to character class:
camtraps$Station_Column <- as.character(camtraps$Station_Column)
camtraps$Camera_Column <- as.character(camtraps$Camera_Column)

It looks as if the error you get for running the surveyReport function might be that you haven't loaded the camtrapR package in your library:
library(camtrapR)

Then try running the surveyReport function again.

I hope this helps,

Best of luck,

Regards,
Philip

messages.subject: Re: Detection history
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
it looks messy but I believe the issue should be solved easily. The problem is highlighted in red:

dethist_vulpes <- detectionHistory(recordTable = vulpes,
                             camOp = cam_operation,
                             stationCol = "Station",
                             speciesCol = "Species",
                             recordDateTimeCol = "DateTimeOriginal",
                             species = "VTA",
                             occasionLength = 1,
                             day1 = "2018-04-03",
                             datesAsOccasionNames = TRUE,
                             includeEffort = TRUE,
                             scaleEffort = FALSE,
                             timeZone = "Australia/Canberra")

This is a bit of leftover code from the function example. Replace it with the species you are interested in, which would be one of unique(vulpes$Species).

speciesCol = "Species" is correct and replacing speciesCol = "Species" with vulpes$Species will not work. Argument speciesCol is the column name, not the species names themselves, and should have length 1. vulpes$Species on the other hand has as many values as the record table has rows, i.e. length(vulpes$Species) = nrow(vulpes). This is what caused the error message:

Error in checkForSpacesInColumnNames(stationCol = stationCol, setupCol = setupCol,  :
  this is a bug in 'checkForSpacesInColumnNames'. I'm sorry. Please report it.

Exiftool is innocent in this case. While it is a good idea to avoid spaces in folder and file names, it should usually work. What really messes up things is special characters in folder names.

Please let me know if the error persists.
Best wishes,
Jürgen
